instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tbsp of the salt.
Cut each chicken breast in half through its thickness, so you have 4 thin cutlets. If one end is still thicker, press it flat with the heel of your hand. Pat them dry with paper towels.
Mix 3/4 tsp of the salt with the 1/2 tsp pepper and the garlic powder, and sprinkle it over both sides of the cutlets.
Spread the 1/3 cup flour on a plate. Press each cutlet into it on both sides and shake off the extra.
Mince the 2 garlic cloves. Drain 1/3 cup of the sun-dried tomatoes and chop them. Chop 2 tbsp of basil and grate 1/2 cup of the parmesan.

Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the butter foams. Add 2 of the cutlets and leave them alone for about 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and lets go of the pan.
Flip them and cook the other side for about 3 minutes, until golden. Transfer them to a plate. Cook the other 2 cutlets the same way with the last 1 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter.
Add the fettuccine to the boiling water and cook it for about 10 minutes, or as the package says, until it's tender with a little bite. Drain it.
Meanwhile, turn the skillet down to medium. Add the garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the 1/2 cup broth and the 1 tsp Dijon. Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom and let it bubble for about 2 minutes, until it's reduced by half.
Turn the heat to medium low. Stir in the 1 cup cream and the last 1/4 tsp salt and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the 3 cups spinach a handful at a time with the sun-dried tomatoes, stirring until the spinach wilts, about 2 minutes.

Return the chicken and its juices to the pan and spoon the sauce over. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon. You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Take the pan off the heat and scatter over the basil.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the chicken and sauce over the fettuccine, with the parmesan at the table.
method_notes: All three sear seasoned chicken breast, deglaze the pan with broth or wine, then simmer it in cream with spinach and sun-dried tomatoes. Salt & Lavender (the lead) slices the breasts into floured cutlets, sears them in oil and butter and adds Dijon to the sauce; Well Plated adds shallot, garlic and Italian seasoning and uses half-and-half, and I Wash You Dry stirs parmesan into the sauce. This follows the lead, adds two cloves of fresh garlic as the other two do, and serves it over fettuccine with parmesan at the table, both suggested by the sources. The honest time is about 40 minutes with the pasta; the lead's 25 is the chicken alone.
